name: Damascus
desc: A billet of pattern-welded steel read as a contour map of its own folding — hundreds of laminated layers cut open by the ground face, the nickel standing proud and bright where the ferric bite has sunk the carbon steel to near-black, while a raking light crawls the plate and the highlight travels band by band.

layers.doc: laminate count across the billet — how many folded layers the ground face exposes

scale.doc: grain of the fold — size of the swirl/wave structure

energy.doc: specular amplitude + depth of the etch relief

density.doc: etch sharpness, surface tooth, and rung/dimple count

hue.doc: re-tints the whole alloy (212 = true blue-grey steel; ~30 reads bronze)

speed.doc: rate of the light crawl and the camera creep across the plate

y.doc: light elevation — where the highlight sits on the band profile

style.doc: etched: ferric-bitten pattern-welded steel, bright nickel over near-black carbon · mokume: mokume-gane, copper/shibuichi/brass laid over black shakudo · nitre: heat-tinted oxide, straw through violet to blue · xray: non-representational — the fold topology alone as bright contour lines on a dark plate, no material at all · ink: sumi, the pattern as brushed tonal bands on paper

pattern.doc: ladder: cut rungs arch the stack · raindrop: drilled dimples ring out · twist: the bar is twisted so the layers go edge-on and open into eyes · wild: unconstrained random damascus

act.doc: forge: the layers keep creeping as if still under the hammer · etch: the acid bite deepens and lifts across sections · polish: low relief, wide hot specular, a faster light

seed.doc: re-forges the billet — new fold field, new rungs, new dimples
